name: Xeround
tagline: Auto-scaling MySQL-compatible cloud DBaaS on a distributed in-memory engine; shut down in May 2013.
description: Xeround was an Israeli company, launched in 2005, whose distributed in-memory database was first sold to telecom operators such as T-Mobile. In 2009 it added a MySQL front end and turned the engine into a cloud database service that promised elastic scaling and high availability without sharding, running on Amazon EC2 and other clouds; the beta reportedly drew about 2,000 organisations and general availability came in June 2011. The business did not pay off: on May 1, 2013 Xeround told paying customers it was closing the service and that data had to be migrated out by May 15, 2013.
statusNote: Service shut down in May 2013 with two weeks' notice to migrate data. Aurora MySQL, PlanetScale or TiDB serve the same need today.

pricing.notes: Historic only; the service no longer exists.

scale.notes: Historically scaled automatically behind a MySQL endpoint.

strengths: Early elastic MySQL-compatible DBaaS without manual sharding (historically)
Distributed in-memory engine with built-in high availability
weaknesses: Service closed in 2013 with only two weeks for customers to migrate
Proprietary engine with no released code
useCases: Case study in DBaaS vendor risk
notIdealFor: Any workload: the service no longer exists
